summary: The study describes the Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) of amorphous lithium borate-carbonate (LBCO) films for solid-state Li metal batteries. The films exhibit high ionic conductivity, up to 2.2 × 10⁻⁶ S cm⁻¹, and are stable against both Li metal anodes and cathode materials. The ALD process uses lithium tert-butoxide, ozone, and triisopropyl borate as precursors, with a temperature range of 200–260 °C. The films show excellent electrochemical stability and are suitable for use as solid electrolytes in thin-film batteries.
evidence: The text states, 'Here we present an Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) process for synthesis of amorphous lithium borate-carbonate (LBCO) films.' It also mentions, 'Lithium tert-butoxide was selected as the lithium source... Ozone was used as the oxidant... Triisopropyl borate was selected as the boron source.' Additionally, 'Substrate temperatures between 200 °C and 260 °C yielded a relatively consistent growth rate.'
